CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness and tingling in fingers and wrist pain, left hand.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male presenting with left wrist and hand pain and numbness that has been ongoing for several months. Symptoms started insidiously without known precipitating event. Patient reports numbness is most prominent at night, often waking with the hand "asleep" and requiring shaking to restore sensation. Numbness affects all fingers but is more pronounced in the thumb and index finger, with occasional involvement of the fifth finger. Patient works in landscaping doing heavy labor with repetitive motions including raking and digging. Denies similar symptoms in the right hand. Reports some associated left hand weakness and difficulty gripping objects, sometimes dropping things due to inability to feel them properly.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies numbness in right hand. No other systemic complaints noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No significant past medical history noted. Denies history of rheumatoid arthritis.

MEDICATIONS
None reported.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works in landscaping performing heavy manual labor with repetitive motions. Denies significant alcohol use, reporting consumption of one to two beers on weekends only.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Cardiovascular: Heart sounds normal. Pulmonary: Lungs clear to auscultation. Grip strength decreased on the left compared to right. Sensation intact bilaterally to light touch on fingers, though patient reports sensation feels slightly abnormal on thumb side of left hand. Bilateral positive Tinel's sign elicited upon percussion of wrists, reproducing tingling sensation in fingertips.

RESULTS
Pending EMG study to evaluate electrical impulses in fingers and confirm carpal tunnel syndrome.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, left more symptomatic than right, likely related to repetitive occupational trauma from landscaping work. Plan includes: (1) Activity modification with delegation of repetitive tasks to other employees for several weeks; (2) Left wrist splint to wear; (3) Ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours; (4) EMG study to be ordered; (5) Follow-up office visit in 2 weeks to reassess symptoms and determine need for further diagnostic testing or possible surgical intervention for nerve decompression.
